title: Solar System & Cosmic Quests
subject: Space & Astronomy
description: Travel across planets, moons, asteroids, and stars in our solar system and beyond.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet' because of iron oxide on its surface?
questions.fact: Mars looks reddish-orange because of rust (iron oxide) in its soil and atmosphere.

questions.question: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.fact: Jupiter is so massive that more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it!

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.fact: Mercury is the smallest planet and closest to the Sun, orbiting it every 88 days.

questions.question: What celestial body is at the exact center of our solar system?
questions.fact: The Sun contains 99.8% of all the mass in the entire solar system!

questions.question: Which planet is famous for having large, bright, visible rings made of ice and dust?
questions.fact: Saturn has thousands of beautiful ringlets composed mostly of chunks of water ice.

questions.question: How long does it take for Earth to complete one full orbit around the Sun?
questions.fact: One Earth year takes about 365 days and 6 hours, which is why we add a leap day every 4 years!

questions.question: What was the name of the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.fact: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the lunar surface on July 20, 1969, saying 'That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.'

questions.question: Which planet is the hottest in our solar system due to a runaway greenhouse effect?
questions.fact: Venus has thick clouds of carbon dioxide and sulfuric acid that trap heat at over 460°C (860°F)!

questions.question: What is the natural satellite of Earth?
questions.fact: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, orbiting about 384,400 km away.

questions.question: Which galaxy do we live in?
questions.fact: The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy containing billions of stars, including our Sun.

questions.question: What is a shooting star really?
options: A meteor burning up in Earth's atmosphere
questions.fact: A shooting star is a small meteoroid burning brightly as it streaks through the atmosphere.

questions.question: Which dwarf planet in our solar system was considered the 9th planet until 2006?
questions.fact: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet by the International Astronomical Union in 2006.

questions.question: What causes day and night on Earth?
questions.fact: As Earth rotates once every 24 hours, different parts face toward or away from the Sun.

questions.question: Which telescope launched into space in 2021 to view the deepest reaches of the universe with infrared light?
questions.fact: The James Webb Space Telescope has a giant gold-plated mirror that captures light from the earliest galaxies!

questions.question: Which planet is tipped on its side and rotates almost completely horizontally?
questions.fact: Uranus has an extreme axial tilt of 98 degrees, so its poles face almost directly at the Sun during parts of its orbit!

questions.question: What is the Great Red Spot on Jupiter?
questions.fact: The Great Red Spot is an enormous anti-cyclonic storm that has been raging for hundreds of years!
